name: Luna 20
short_status: Success: returned about 55 g from the Apollonius highlands, 14 to 25 February 1972, the first sample of lunar highland soil brought back by a robot.
tagline: Soviet Union · Sample return · 1972 · The space race Success
stats: anorthosite grains, the first robotic highland soil
robotic sample return in history, after Luna 16
from Baikonur launch to sample capsule on Earth

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 14 February 1972, 03:27:58 UTC, Proton from Tyuratam (Baikonur Cosmodrome)

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion
facts.value: 18 February 1972, into an approximately 100 x 100 km orbit at 65 degrees inclination

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 21 February 1972, soft-landed in the Apollonius highlands near Mare Fecunditatis, about 120 km from where Luna 16 had landed

facts.label: Landing coordinates
facts.value: 3.7863 N, 56.6242 E, as listed in the NSSDCA Master Catalog

facts.label: Sample
facts.value: About 55 g of loosely compacted highland soil collected by a 90 cm extendable drill arm (Vinogradov, 1972); NSSDCA states 30 g and the Lunar Sample Compendium about 50 g

facts.label: Composition
facts.value: 50 to 60% of the rock particles were ancient anorthosite (feldspar-rich highland crust), unlike Luna 16's mare basalt with roughly 1 to 2% anorthosite

facts.label: Ascent
facts.value: 22 February 1972, the 520 kg ascent stage fired its single-burn KRD-61 engine (one 53-second firing) for a direct ascent trajectory to Earth

facts.label: Earth return
facts.value: 25 February 1972 at 19:19 UT, the capsule parachuted onto an island in the Karkingir River, about 40 km N of Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: Ye-8-5 bus, 3.96 m tall; 1,880 kg dry landed mass, 5,600 to 5,750 kg fueled at launch; return capsule 50 cm diameter, 39 kg

facts.label: The failed predecessor
facts.value: Luna 18 crashed into the same highland border on 11 September 1971 (signals ceased at impact in mountainous terrain), five months before Luna 20 landed nearby and succeeded

facts.label: Sample exchange with NASA
facts.value: March 1973: NASA traded 3 g each of Apollo 16 and Apollo 17 material for portions of the Luna 16 and Luna 20 samples

facts.label: LROC imaging
facts.value: The Luna 20 descent stage was photographed by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter on 30 January 2010 (NAC frame M119482862RE); the shadow of the sampling arm is visible

timeline: Luna 18, the previous sample-return attempt, crashes in the same highland border region; its signals stop at impact
Enters an approximately 100 km circular lunar orbit at 65 degrees inclination
Soft-lands in the Apollonius highlands, ~120 km from Luna 16; the drill collects about 55 g of anorthositic soil
Ascent stage lifts off the Moon with the sealed sample capsule on a direct trajectory home
Capsule lands at 19:19 UT on an island in the Karkingir River near Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan, with the first robotic highland sample
Apollo 16 lands at Descartes, the first crewed mission dedicated to the lunar highlands, sampling the terrain Luna 20 had just previewed
NASA and the USSR exchange samples: 6 g of Apollo material for portions of the Luna 16 and Luna 20 soil
LROC publishes orbital images pinpointing the Luna 20 descent stage in the highlands, with the sampling-arm shadow visible
